chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ibn Abi Umayr and Fadala from Jamil ibn Darradj said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman who arrives in Mecca on the Day of Tawreeq. He said: 'She proceeds as she is to Arafat and makes it her Hajj, then she stays until she becomes pure, and goes out to Al-Tan'eem, puts on Ihram, and makes it an Umrah.'
Ibn Abi Umayr said: 'As Aisha did.'

key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat (site of the main Hajj ritual)
key_terms.يَوْمَ اَلتَّرْوِيَةِ: Day of Tawreeq (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What should a menstruating woman do if she arrives in Mecca on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah before performing ritual purification?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the precedent of performing Hajj in a state of menstruation, a ruling derived from the Prophet's companion Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who was menstruating during the Farewell Pilgrimage. The Imam instructs her to complete the Hajj rites in Mecca and then perform Umrah from Al-Tan'eem after purification, effectively compensating for the missed Umrah. This ruling highlights the Shia view that menstruation does not invalidate the core pillars of Hajj, only requiring a separate Umrah for completion.
